A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 20-page versions of the same GENIE paper. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermarking, model-extraction, robustness, ownership-piracy, and runtime experiments, including additional results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds NeoGNN evaluations and a detailed comparison of watermark embedding methods.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 replaces owner-supplied thresholds at dispute time with pre-training registration, judge-generated watermarks, and judge-computed thresholds. Section 5.6 also proposes output inversion for selected links as an adaptive-attack defense. The underlying watermark construction and alternating training updates remain substantially unchanged; DWT largely reproduces v1's Appendix C threshold procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven primary graph datasets and retain Router, ogbl-collab, and Wikipedia in the appendices. NeoGNN adds a model configuration, not dataset or task coverage. The adaptive-attack section supplies no experimentally evaluated new scenario.

E2.justification: v1 briefly compares data poisoning and summed losses in Section 6, footnote 8. v2's Section 5.3 and Table 5 expand this into an explicit four-baseline GCN comparison, adding Xu et al.'s fine-tuning approach and MGDA alongside data poisoning and Uniform Loss. The existing watermark-removal comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds NeoGNN evaluation with a 256-dimensional, three-layer GCN/MLP configuration trained for 400 epochs, and specifies 50 epochs for the new embedding fine-tuning baseline. Efficiency assessment shifts from measured training times to trigger-size ratios. Existing splits, AUC evaluation, and retained attack protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The brief embedding-rule analysis in v1's Section 6 becomes a systematic seven-dataset GCN ablation in v2's Section 5.3 and Table 5, with additional alternatives and detailed utility and watermark scores. Existing robustness and piracy analyses are retained across relocation. Section 5.6 discusses adaptive attacks without reporting a new empirical robustness test.

E5.justification: Both retain ten-seed averages with plus/minus reporting, the same hypothesis-testing approach, 100,000 smoothed-bootstrap samples, and KDE threshold simulations illustrated with one million samples. DWT re-presents the existing threshold procedure, and NeoGNN results follow the established statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds NeoGNN thresholds, benchmark scores, and per-model statistical results in Tables 3, 4, and A.4, plus detailed embedding-comparison results in Table 5. For example, newly reported NeoGNN arXiv scores are 99.92% clean-test, 99.91% watermarked-test, and 94.22% watermark AUC. v1's Table 15 runtime results disappear. Matched retained benchmark and attack table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The trust assumptions change from an owner truthfully supplying thresholds to judge-generated watermarks and judge-calculated thresholds. Section 5.6 introduces explicit assumptions about an adaptive adversary's knowledge and a node-ID query interface. The statistical hypotheses and KDE error-rate argument remain substantially unchanged, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 adds an adaptive-attacker defense to its main contributions and explicitly extends DWT's claimed applicability to other accuracy/AUC-based watermarking schemes. The first GNN link-prediction watermarking claim, functionality-preservation and robustness claims, and FPR/FNR bound remain. Renaming thresholding and foregrounding the existing embedding procedure do not establish new algorithms.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of threshold generality and adaptive-attack resistance, explains piracy resolution through registration timestamps, and replaces timing-based efficiency discussion with a trigger-size argument. It removes v1's explicit static-graph and transductive-setting limitations and its warning about lacking guarantees against future attacks. The adaptive-defense claims are not backed by reported experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds NeoGNN implementation settings and watermarking rates. It also discloses SEAL rates of 3% for arXiv and 4% for PPI, replacing dashes in v1's Table A.1 despite those evaluations already being reported. Measured training times are removed; existing hardware, optimizer, learning rates, and training budgets are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around inefficient threshold procedures, false ownership claims, and adaptive attacks in Sections 1 and 4.3.2. New citations include False Claims Against Model Ownership Resolution, GROVE, Neo-GNNs, and MGDA. Several general deep-learning and non-DNN link-prediction background references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around MLaaS and ownership demonstration, background material is compressed, and watermark verification receives a new subsection structure. The discussion/limitations section is removed, while implementation details, threshold explanation, piracy analysis, and appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adds an embedding-comparison table, a NeoGNN statistical table, and a dataset-statistics table, while widening Tables 3 and 4 for NeoGNN. It removes the runtime table and overview diagram. The existing KDE figure moves into the main text, while piracy plots and three GCN fine-pruning tables move into the appendices, substantially changing the presentation.

improvement.justification: Table 5 and the NeoGNN results strengthen empirical support, and Appendix B fills missing implementation details. However, v2 removes measured runtime evidence and explicit applicability limitations. Its new Section 4.4 says Dwm is written to a public bulletin board, while Section 5.6 relies on Dwm remaining secret. This unresolved security contradiction, together with the untested adaptive defense, prevents a reliable net quality judgment despite the empirical gains.
